title: Hadamard Maximal Determinant
tagline: +1s and -1s in a grid. Maximize the determinant.
description: Given n, find an n x n matrix with entries in {+1, -1} whose determinant is larger than any known construction. Solved exactly for n <= 22. Open for every n >= 23 where the best known construction falls below the theoretical bound.
context: Hadamard (1893): if every entry of a matrix is +1 or -1, how large can the determinant be? For n <= 22, the answer is known exactly after over a century of work. For n = 23 onwards, the best constructions come from hill-climbing searches run by Orrick et al. in 2003. Many of those records have stood for 20+ years. Every n with a gap between the current record and the theoretical ceiling is independently attackable.
verification: Exact integer determinant via sympy. No floating point. Accepts if |det(M)| strictly exceeds the current record for that n.

howToStart.title: Pick an n
howToStart.body: Any row in the table. n=23 is the smallest open case.

howToStart.title: Random start
howToStart.body: Generate a random {+1,-1} matrix. Compute its determinant.

howToStart.title: Hill-climb
howToStart.body: Flip entries that increase |det|. Cofactor expansion lets you update cheaply without recomputing from scratch.

howToStart.title: Simulated annealing
howToStart.body: Perturb when stuck. This is exactly how the 2003 records were set.

bounds.name: Hadamard bound
bounds.formula: n^(n/2). Tight when a Hadamard matrix exists.

bounds.name: Ehlich's bound
bounds.formula: Derived from eigenvalue analysis of M^T M
